02 / Tack · UI & UX update

Make room for the work.

A smaller header and earlier capture keep the board at the center of the experience.

606 → 333 pxCapture start in the In progress column.

Compact heading. Larger card text. Capture before the list. Secondary actions under Options.

Same six cards, same viewport. Rounded CSS pixels. These are layout measurements, not measured time savings. The baseline’s development indicator is not app UI.

Capture is visible on a phone.

A labeled New card action stays in the header. Filters collapse, while active choices stay visible.

Smaller screens show one chosen status at a time. Desktop shows all four columns from 1180 px.

04 / Tack · UI & UX update

Know what saved. Keep what didn’t.

A failed edit stays in the editor with a clear choice: Retry save or Discard changes.

  • Close and Archive wait for the latest text.
  • Copying a link has its own confirmation.
  • Recovered issue drafts are reviewed before saving.
  • Keyboard focus stays within the dialog and returns to the task.

Draft recovery is scoped to the same tab and account, for up to 24 hours. It does not provide offline sync or cross-user conflict resolution.

05 / Tack · UI & UX update

Keep the user’s chosen view.

An empty column can be the right place to work.

The selected Ready column stays selected even when the current search matches a card elsewhere.

  • Search and filters stay visible and removable.
  • Creating a card retains the current filters.
  • A hidden new card gets a persistent Show card / Clear filters notice.
  • Shared card links retain their context through sign-in.

Shown: U2 filtered-empty view on the original six-card board. This screenshot demonstrates retained selection; the hidden-new-card notice is a separate tested state.

06 / Tack · UI & UX update

A failure now has a next step.

Keep the input, explain the uncertainty, and offer recovery beside the task.

Shared updates and saved changes have separate status.

Retry refresh addresses an out-of-date board. Retry action or Check board addresses a move that could not be confirmed.

Failed capture keeps the title and avoids automatic resubmission. Expired sessions offer sign-in in another tab.

A lost response can leave a write’s outcome uncertain. Retained input and checking the board support a deliberate retry.

07 / Tack · UI & UX update

Make account changes understandable.

Pending, failure, and success messages stay beside the affected account.

  • Password changes offer Cancel.
  • Protected-account reasons are visible without hover.
  • New-account feedback stays at the creation form.
  • Label removal explains its effect on every card before confirmation.

Existing permissions remain in place. Passwords are not copied to browser storage.

08 / Tack · UI & UX update

Verified locally. Ready for pilot preparation.

51browser checks passed5 intentional skips
20domain / export / return-path checks passed

Additional confidence

Lint, TypeScript, and production build passed. Automated accessibility scans passed in the tested board, editor, labels, and Team states.

Final production inspection found no page errors or horizontal overflow in the checked views. The original six cards were unchanged.

What the pilot must establish

Whether people can capture, find, and move cards without help—and whether they trust saved and shared state.

Real-device, Firefox/WebKit, screen-reader, and representative-user coverage remain unverified. This is not an accessibility-conformance claim.

After feedback cleanup: 31 focused checks passed, 1 duplicate skipped; final label-focus checks: 4 passed. These overlap earlier runs and are not additive. Recorded application results from U3-DELIVERY.md; the suite was not rerun for this presentation.

09 / Tack · UI & UX update

The next decision is the pilot.

Keep the product boundary simple: Backlog → Ready → In progress → Done.

01

Name the people

Choose a pilot owner, operations contact, participants, dates, and feedback-log location.

02

Prepare the service

Choose the TLS host and off-host backups. Deploy, verify health, complete a restore drill, and inspect an export.

03

Observe for two weeks

Introduce the workflow in ten minutes. Check on days 2, 7, and 14. Record friction and repeated workarounds.

04

Choose from evidence

Address operational defects immediately. At the review, select at most one next product improvement.

The UI/UX upgrade is complete locally.
The next evidence should come from the team using it.
